{"consolidated_memory":"storage/sql/migrations/0042_add_index.sql has experienced recurring lock timeout problems with the same error signal (lock wait that trips statement timeout) but four distinct root causes and fixes across different scenarios:

OCCASION 1 [2026-01-20]:
- Trigger: Only occurred for accounts in the five percent rollout bucket
- Root cause: N+1 query hidden behind a lazy relation
- Measured outcome: Cold start performance degraded by 98 percent to 813 ms
- Fix: Prefetched the relation in a single query
- PR #5064, branch fix/lock-timeout-1

OCCASION 2 [2026-03-07]:
- Trigger: Only occurred when the input list came in empty
- Root cause: Unbounded retry loop with no backoff
- Measured outcome: 50 duplicate rows per day stopped being written
- Fix: Capped the retry attempts and added exponential backoff with jitter
- PR #6606, branch fix/lock-timeout-2

OCCASION 3 [2026-03-12]:
- Trigger: Only occurred for sessions that arrived through the OAuth provider
- Root cause: Off-by-one error in the slice bound
- Measured outcome: Flaky test improved from 99 failures per 100 runs to zero
- Fix: Corrected the slice bound and added a property test around it
- PR #9178, branch fix/lock-timeout-3

OCCASION 4 [2026-08-27]:
- Trigger: Only occurred for traffic arriving through the corporate proxy
- Root cause: Connection pool exhaustion under burst load
- Measured outcome: Error rate dropped from 5.0 percent to under 5 per 10,000
- Fix: Raised the pool ceiling and put a bounded wait queue in front of it
- PR #9926, branch fix/lock-timeout-4

Common reproduction: Run the migration against a loaded table. All work was on the storage side in the same corner of the file, with context carrying over between fixes."}
